q: Anas (RA) described what the Prophet ﷺ broke his fast with before praying. What was his order of preference?
o: Water, then dried dates, then fresh dates
Milk, then fresh dates, then bread
Fresh dates, then dried dates, then water
Dried dates, then milk, then water
x: He ﷺ broke his fast with fresh dates (rutab) before praying; if there were none, with dried dates; and if there were none, with a few sips of water.

q: The Prophet ﷺ told Abdullah ibn Amr (RA) to fast three days each month. He said that is like fasting for how long?
x: He ﷺ said: Fast three days a month, for a good deed is rewarded ten times over, and that is like fasting the whole year. A simple way to keep fasting after Ramadan.

q: Quran 2:183 tells the believers that fasting has been prescribed for them. How does the verse end: 'so that you may...'?
x: The verse ends 'la'allakum tattaqun': so that you may become righteous, gaining taqwa (mindfulness of Allah). The Quran names this as the purpose of fasting.

q: In Quran 2:187, believers may eat and drink at night until what becomes distinct to them?
o: The first rays of the rising sun
The white thread of dawn from the black thread
The last light of the moon
x: Allah says: Eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread of night. Then complete the fast until the night.

q: The Prophet ﷺ said the fasting person has two joys. One is when he breaks his fast. When is the other?
x: There are two joys for the fasting person: one when he breaks his fast, and one when he meets his Lord, when he will be pleased because of his fasting.

q: The Prophet ﷺ spoke of gates of Paradise for the people of prayer, fasting and charity. Abu Bakr (RA) asked if anyone is called from all of them. What was the reply?
o: No, each person has only one gate
Yes, and I hope you will be one of them
Only those who fasted every day
x: Abu Hurairah (RA) reported that the people of fasting will be called from the gate of ar-Rayyan. When Abu Bakr (RA) asked about all the gates, he ﷺ said: Yes, and I hope you will be one of them.

q: The Prophet ﷺ said people will remain upon goodness as long as they do what?
o: Delay iftar until the stars appear
x: Sahl ibn Sa'd (RA) reported that he ﷺ said: The people will remain upon goodness as long as they hasten to break the fast. So do not delay iftar once its time has come.

q: Ibn Abbas (RA) said the Prophet ﷺ prescribed zakat al-fitr as a purification for the fasting person from what?
x: He ﷺ prescribed it to purify the fasting person from idle and obscene talk, and as food for the poor. Given before the Eid prayer, it is accepted as zakat.

q: The Prophet ﷺ said prayer in congregation is superior to praying alone by how many degrees?
x: Ibn Umar (RA) reported: Prayer in congregation is twenty-seven degrees superior to prayer offered by a person alone.

q: The Prophet ﷺ asked: if a river ran by your door and you bathed in it five times a day, would any dirt remain? What was he describing?
x: The Companions said no dirt would remain. He ﷺ said: That is the example of the five prayers, with which Allah wipes away sins.

q: In Ramadan, more and more people gathered to pray behind the Prophet ﷺ at night. Why did he then stop coming out to them?
o: He was too ill to lead them
He feared it would be made obligatory
He was away on a journey
x: Aishah (RA) reported he said: I saw what you did, and nothing stopped me from coming out to you except that I feared it would be made obligatory on you. That was in Ramadan.

q: Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b (RA) asked the Prophet ﷺ for his company in Paradise. What did the Prophet ﷺ tell him to do to help reach it?
x: Rabi'ah (RA), who brought him water for wudu at night, said: I ask for your company in Paradise. He ﷺ said: Then help me to achieve this for you by making many prostrations.

q: Which prayer did the Prophet ﷺ call the best prayer after the obligatory prayers?
x: Abu Hurairah (RA) reported: The best fasting after Ramadan is in Allah's month, Muharram, and the best prayer after the obligatory prayer is the prayer at night.

q: The Prophet ﷺ would stand in night prayer until his feet swelled. When asked why, what did he say?
o: I like the quiet of the night
Should I not be a thankful servant?
I want to finish the whole Quran
The angels told me to do so
x: Al-Mughirah (RA) reported that he prayed until his feet swelled, and when asked about it he said: Should I not be a thankful servant?

q: The first thing a person will be brought to account for is the prayer. If their obligatory prayers are lacking, what completes them?
x: Allah will say: See whether My servant has any voluntary prayers. If he has, the obligatory prayers are completed with them. A strong reason to keep up the Sunnah prayers.

q: Quran 29:45 says prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing. What does the verse then say is greater?
x: Allah says: Establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater. And Allah knows what you do.

q: Which surah did the Prophet ﷺ call the greatest surah in the Quran?
x: He ﷺ told Abu Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla (RA) that Al-Hamdu lillahi Rabbil-'alamin is the greatest surah: the seven oft-repeated verses and the Grand Quran given to him.

q: The Prophet ﷺ asked Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA) which verse in the Book of Allah is the greatest. Which verse did Ubayy name?
x: Ubayy (RA), known as Abu al-Mundhir, answered: Allah, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. The Prophet ﷺ tapped him on the chest and said: May knowledge be pleasant for you, Abu al-Mundhir.

q: A man heard someone repeating Surah al-Ikhlas over and over and told the Prophet ﷺ, as if he thought it too little. What did the Prophet ﷺ say it is equal to?
x: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (RA) reported that he ﷺ said: By Him in Whose Hand my soul is, it is equal to one-third of the Quran.

q: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever recites a letter of Allah's Book earns a good deed. How many times is that good deed multiplied?
x: Ibn Mas'ud (RA) reported: each good deed is multiplied by ten. I do not say Alif Lam Mim is one letter; Alif is a letter, Lam is a letter and Mim is a letter.

q: The Prophet ﷺ likened the believer who recites the Quran to a citron (utrujjah). Why a citron?
o: It tastes good and smells good
x: Abu Musa (RA) reported that he ﷺ said: the believer who recites the Quran is like a citron, good in smell and taste; the believer who does not recite it is like a date, sweet but without smell.

q: How long did the Prophet ﷺ first tell Abdullah ibn Amr (RA) to take to recite the whole Quran?
x: He ﷺ said: Recite the whole Quran in one month. When Abdullah said he had strength for more, he said: Then recite it in seven days.

q: A man reciting Surah al-Kahf saw a cloud come closer and closer over him, and his horse grew restless. What did the Prophet ﷺ say it was?
o: A storm cloud about to burst
Dust stirred up by the desert wind
Tranquility sent down with the Quran
x: Al-Bara (RA) reported that the man told the Prophet ﷺ about it the next morning, and he said: That was the sakinah (tranquility), which came down because of the Quran.

q: Which of these statements does Allah repeat four times in Surah al-Qamar?
o: The Quran was sent down in Ramadan
We have made the Quran easy for remembrance
The Quran is healing for the believers
Recite the Quran with measured recitation
x: Allah says in 54:17, 22, 32 and 40: And We have certainly made the Quran easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?

q: Surah al-Qadr says the Night of Decree is peace until when?
o: The last third of the night
x: Allah says: Peace it is until the emergence of dawn (97:5). The night stays a night of peace until Fajr breaks, so keep striving until then.

q: According to Surah al-Qadr, who descend on the Night of Decree by permission of their Lord?
x: Allah says: The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord for every matter (97:4). The Spirit here is Jibreel.

q: Surah al-Qadr says the Quran was sent down on the Night of Decree. Which other surah says it was sent down 'during a blessed night'?
x: Allah says in Surah ad-Dukhan: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night (44:3), and in Surah al-Qadr: We sent it down during the Night of Decree (97:1).

q: The Prophet ﷺ came out to tell the people the date of Laylatul Qadr, but knowledge of it was taken away. Why?
o: He was called away on a journey
x: He ﷺ said: I came out to tell you about Laylatul Qadr, but so-and-so and so-and-so quarrelled, so it was taken away, and perhaps that is better for you.

q: Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA) mentioned a sign the Prophet ﷺ gave for the morning after Laylatul Qadr. What is it?
o: The sun rises white, without rays
A red moon rises at dawn
x: Ubayy (RA) said the sign the Prophet ﷺ told them of is that the sun rises on the morning after it white, without rays.

q: Abu Hurairah (RA) said the Prophet ﷺ used to do i'tikaf for ten days every Ramadan. How many days did he do in the year he passed away?
x: Abu Hurairah (RA) said he ﷺ used to do i'tikaf for ten days every Ramadan, and in the year he passed away he did i'tikaf for twenty days.

q: Seeking Laylatul Qadr, the Prophet ﷺ did i'tikaf in the first ten days of Ramadan, then the middle ten. What was he then told?
o: It is in the month of Shawwal
It is in the last ten nights
It is on the first night
It is on the night of Eid
x: Abu Sa'id (RA) reported he said: I did i'tikaf in the first ten seeking this night, then in the middle ten. Then I was told it is in the last ten.

q: During i'tikaf in the masjid, the Prophet ﷺ would lean his head into the house to Aishah (RA). Why?
o: To see if the moon had risen
So she could comb his hair
x: Aishah (RA) said: he would put his head in to me while he was in the masjid, and I would comb his hair. In i'tikaf he would not enter the house except for a need.
